subject: Fix next_action workspace pinning: evaluate each loop against its own workspace graph
description: Bug in /Users/imyu/Desktop/cloude/orchestrator/daemon.js (same checkout as ~/.claude/orchestrator): the loop registry entries (loop_start) store no workspace, and the next_action heartbeat computes ready/running/drained against the daemon's GLOBAL state.workspace. Reproduced 2026-06-10: another session flipped state.workspace mid-run; the heartbeat for loop 3cdd8fde-4fbf-4735-b893-94c9e70908f5 then saw a 0-task graph and returned action:"stop", reason "DAG drained (nothing ready, running, or externally pending)", demoting an active loop whose own workspace (/Users/imyu/Desktop/cloude) had ready+running tasks. Fix: capture the requesting session's workspace on loop_start (the daemon already receives a workspace pin on mutating POSTs via mcp-core makeCall), persist it on the loop entry (loops.json), and have decideOne/next_action load THAT loop's workspace graph instead of the global one. The /workspace global pointer should remain only a default for unpinned loops. Also consider: the stale-claim sweep (stale_minutes, default 10) releases claims of long-running workers that never touch lastChanged mid-task — evaluate refreshing lastChanged when an agent is still registered as running, or document that workers must re-claim. Add regression coverage in test/ (smoke.sh has loop/next-action end-to-end checks). Work in an isolated worktree branch off ~/.claude/orchestrator (orch/attempt/<slug>), never merge to main, complete_task with MERGE PENDING. If a PreToolUse gate blocks direct edits, write to /tmp and cp into place.
